CHIEF COMPLAINT
Nonhealing foot ulcer

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a patient with a two-month history of a foot ulcer on the right foot. The ulcer initially appeared after the patient walked barefoot on Dewey Beach. Over the past two months, the ulcer has become increasingly problematic, with recent onset of redness and drainage, which prompted the patient to seek care. The patient reports the ulcer sometimes throbs but denies severe localized pain, though notes increased pressure sensation. The patient's primary concern is the new drainage and erythema. The patient was seen by their primary care physician prior to this visit and was prescribed antibiotics; however, the patient has not yet filled this prescription and cannot recall the specific antibiotic name. The patient has a history of diabetes, which is believed to be a significant contributing factor to poor ulcer healing.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports occasional throbbing in the foot. Denies fever. No other systems reviewed documented in visit.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Diabetes mellitus

MEDICATIONS
Patient reports taking diabetes medication but does not consistently monitor blood sugar levels. Unclear which specific diabetes medications patient is currently taking. PCP prescribed antibiotics (name unknown, not yet filled).

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works as an ambulance driver. Recent activity includes walking barefoot at Dewey Beach.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Normal, no fever
Foot exam: One by two inch circular wound on the dorsal aspect of the lateral right foot, just proximal to the fifth metatarsal-phalangeal joint. Erythema present. Drainage present. Edema noted around the wound. No necrosis visualized. No odor appreciated. No bony exposure. Patient reports increased pressure sensation but denies distinct pain with palpation.

RESULTS
Right foot X-ray: No evidence of osteomyelitis

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Diabetic foot ulcer with infection: Start clindamycin 400 mg orally twice daily for seven days. Perform debridement to remove devitalized tissue. Order ankle-brachial index (ABI) to assess lower extremity blood supply and healing potential. Provide surgical shoe to wear for the next month to minimize pressure and irritation to the foot. Follow up in two weeks for possible repeat debridement and reassessment of tissue healing.
2. Diabetes management: Encourage patient to follow up with PCP for diabetes treatment plan optimization. Patient reports last A1C approximately 10, which is elevated. Stress importance of improved glycemic control for ulcer healing.
3. Patient instructed to call office with any concerns between visits. If fever develops or any signs of systemic infection occur, patient instructed to go to urgent care or emergency department.
